Life Esidimeni revisited

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Link:
As part of a program to deinstitutionalize mentally ill patients and cut costs between the 1st of April and the 30th of June 2016, the Gauteng MEC for Health Qedani Mahlangu moved an estimated 1371 mentally ill patients from Life Esidimeni to 27 NGO’s and various hospitals with catastrophic results. When we brought you the story last July we were shocked by what we had uncovered, but the findings released by the health Ombud on the 1st of February this year have left South Africa silenced. 94 mentally ill patients have died, due to a series of events that could have largely been avoided. And now we are asking who will be held accountable?

Broll of Catherine:
Voice over: In our first story we met Catherine whose Sister Virginia was one of the patients who lost their lives after being moved from Life Esidimeni

Up sound: (How they couldn’t find her sister and then they found her and how their were 6 other bodies there)

Link: After speaking to Catherine we went to the MEC for health in Gauteng and told her that there were 6 people reported dead at Precious Angel Care, one of the NGO’s where patients from Life Esidimeni had been moved.

Upsound from MEC

Link: But according to the health Ombuds report there have now been 20 deaths at Precious angel care (how many were after we left the MEC)
After investigations started into Precious Angel Care The owner closed down the NGO in the middle of the night and is currently not contactable

Prof:
1. Precious Angel care what does he know?
2. In July we knew of 6 deaths from Precious Angel care, now there are 20. When were the other deaths?
3. How many patients dead and where?
4. When interviewing the key members of the department what answers was he given about deaths?
5. How many died from actually mental illness related causes
6. Like in Christine’s case how many cases were there where people lost for how long and found in the morg?
7. Other discrepancies about deaths?





Minister of Health
1. What was the policy MEC was implementing? What went wrong?
2. Why the haste?
3. But in 2015 the MEC had in fact underspent on her budget, so why the need to cut costs?

Link: We asked the MEC herself the same questions in July 2016 and this was her response:
MEC up sound about cost saving

Link: In June 2015 The South African Society of Psychiatrists wrote to the MEC about the risks of this move, calling it “premature” In November 2015, sadag and the families of the patients met with the department and asked them to slow down and follow procedure. In December 2015 after litigation action The gauteng department of Health agreed to consultation and to put the patients safety first. But In March 2016 the department started moving patients to Takalani

Mark Section 21

1. What was the litigation taken in March 2016 against the department?
2. The courts ruled in their favor? Why?
3. From the ombuds report though we now know that 15 patients died at Takalani?
4. How many times did the families meet with the department?
5. After the move where concerns clearly expressed to the MEC?
6. So the MEC and the department of health had been clearly warned about the repercussions of this move?
7. Was this avoidable?

Voice over:
In our story last year we managed to go undercover into to two of the 27 NGO’s where collectively … patients were being housed. We found that the nGO’s had not been paid – upsound. That the clinics in the area were ill prepared for the influx of patients and the owner of the NGO was actually battling to get the patients medication, resulting in one patient we met having a full relapse and landed up in Bara

Upsound from – with image

VO: The second NGO we managed to get a spy camera into was Bophelong in Hammenskraal, which is in fact registered to the same owner as Precious Angel care. Here we found

VO: Reverend… son was a patient at Bophelong
His story

VO: Like precious Angel Care Bophelong has been closed down by its owner.

Link: In July of 2016 we confronted the MEC herself an the state of these NGO’s
MEC interview


Link: The health Ombuds report directly contradicts what the MEC told us during that interview:
Prof’s interview:
1. The MEC told us that the NGO’s had been evaluated by her team?
2. Criteria of evaluation of the NGO’s ?
3. 27 NGO were all illegal – how
4. From July 2016 when this was flagged by the media to when your report was released how many deaths have there been?
5. Could this have been avoided? How?
6. In your report who must be held accountable and how?
7. How many people are still being housed in NGO’s ? what was your recommendation?

Minister of Health
1. What will happen to the MEC now that she has already resigned?
2. And the HOD Dr Tiego Ephraim Selebano and Dr. Manamela?
3. Besides all the human rights violations, they forged documents to get these NGO’s licenses. Why this urgency?
4. What was the hurry? Why did they need to make this move so urgently 94 people had to die?
5. What is happening to the people that are still in these NGO’s?
6. What do we say now to the 1000’s of families that sent email after email to Manamela and the MEC begging for them to help with their distressed family members?







Mark from Section 27
1. What legal action if any will Section 27 be taking moving forward and against whom?
2. The unlicensed NGO’s is that a potential fraud case against Dr Manamela
3. What about the patients who are still in the NGO’s?
4. Mark in your opinion was this avoidable?

Catherine and The Reverend
1. Feelings now that the report has been released? What do you want now?

Press Release:


State Mental Patient Death Toll
In June last year the Department of Health cancelled its contract with Life Esidimeni, a facility that took care of mentally ill state patients. Almost 2000 patients were subsequently transferred to several under-equipped NGOs. In September Carte Blanche exposed the deaths of several patients under the care of these NGOs and brought this to the attention of Gauteng Health MEC, Qedani Mahlangu. This week a report revealed that a staggering 94 psychiatric patients had in fact died of unnatural causes at these facilities. Devastated families and supporters are now demanding to know who is responsible.


Script:


Duration Character
00:00 – 00:28 Christine: My sister’s name was Virginia; on Thursday the 25th of August I received a call from a lady called Ethel. She told me she was a director of precious Angel Care, and she was telling me that my sister was no more; she was no more and passed away.
00:28- 00:48 Rev: Lilly was sort of a mental psychiatric patient for quite a very long time. Bill was moved in June and was moved to Hammeskraal. He passed away on 22nd of July only the devil knows what happened.
00:48 – 01:12 V/O Devi Devi: Between the 1st of April and 30th of June 2016, the Gauteng MEC for Health Qedani Mahlangu moved an estimated 1371 mentally ill patients from Life Esidimeni to 27 NGO and various hospitals with disastrous consequences. We reported on this back in September 2016.
01:12 – 01:41 Devi interview Devi: So most people are asking what was wrong with Life Esidimeni what went wrong with that relationship or what was the departments thinking?
MEC: I think firstly we had to move from institutionalize arrangements to community based care. Secondly the issues of using the resources much more efficient was the factor, we were paying about R9000, R9900 OR so per patient at life and that was becoming extremely costly
01:41 – 01:52 Devi: When we broke this story in September last year at that stage we were aware of 36 deaths. But the numbers contained in the health ombudsman report has left the country in shock.
01:52-02:04 Rev: A total of 94 and not 36 mentally ill patients have died during this process.
02:04 Devi: on the 13th of September 2016 were the MEC for health in Gauteng announced that 36 patients had passed away. The ombudsman report proves that in fact 77 had already died.
: Section 27 Mark: its almost easy to say 94 people died and then you think ‘okay they died “people die it happens quickly. Now these are people who died slowly who died painfully, who died often without anybody to ask or provide them with help? There was no body standing over them torturing them but the affect of what was happening they were being tortured.
02:38 Devi: Christine Nxumalo was informed of his sisters passing almost 10 days after she had died, last year she was fighting for answers form the NGO where her sister had been placed.
02:48 Christine: We asked Ethel if she could give us the address so we could go to the facility and to Precious Angel Care she basically didn’t give it to us.

02:57 Christine on the phone with Ethel Christine: Ethel I want to see where my sister died. I want to see the room where she was in I want to see the condition of the place where she was staying
03:07 Devi: After being denied access to the NGO where her sister passed away Christine began the search to find the body she was told it was at a mortuary in Arch Ridgeville but when she arrived it was clearly not there. Eventually she located her sister in a mortuary in Soshenguve.
03:26 Christine: we did see her; we did see her and she looked peaceful yeah
03:33 Devi: At the mortuary Christine discovered there were 6 more bodied from Precious Angels which is information we shared with MEC back in 2016
03:43 Devi interview from 2016 with MEC Devi: So I have got another case study, have you come across the Angel Care Facility in Atridgeville? That apparently there were 6 bodies that came specifically over a period of time and this place was opened in June from Precious Angel Care. You are not aware of this? Never popped up?
MEC: well I know about the Precious angle but the fact that 6 patience who died or one that got lost, the undertaker says patients came in there. We will investigate and come to the bottom of it.
04:10 Devi: The health’s ombudsman Professor Maqoba was appointed to an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of mentally ill patients in Gauteng and advice the way forward.
04:22 Prof: 73 voices that came to give evidence that the action that followed for this project okay was chaotic it was hurried; it was in a rush it was shambolic.
04:33 Devi: The ombudsman report confirmed that there were 20 patients dead at Precious Angel and nothing was done by the MEC. Yet we informed her in August last year, in fact action was only take by the Minister of Health in October
04:48 Minister: I immediately sent the ministerial advice committee of Mental Health. Within 48 hours they had visited 17 NGO’s. All we are saying is go to the NGO look, if you have got any idling that tomorrow more people might die close it.
Devi: because you have to act quickly.
Minister: yes, I had to act quickly. Precious Angels remember that’s where 20 people died so within that 48 hours they closed it
05:18 Devi: During our previous investigation we got hidden camera into some of the NGO were we found there was no space for any recreational activities. A serve lack of food and medication and the most was the NGO’s complained of not being paid by the department even though the patients had been there for 3 months. Bophelong was were Reverend Joseph son Billy was placed.
05:40 Rev: The NGO was not really a conducive place to keep psychiatric patients. Billy and the others didn’t have enough food, there was no medication, and also there was no toilets and they used to pig toilet, he was filthy, he was hungry, he was dehydrated, and he was cold. When we went to pick up his body on they said he had an infection on his lungs before then he was not sick. When he was in Esidimeni he was not sick, he was okay.
06:15 Devi: We informed the MEC of the issues back in August 2016.
06:20 Devi: do you feel that it was a smooth transaction, the patients that have been moved to NGO are they happy are they settled?
MEC: from where I’m sitting I think we did our best in managing the situation and I think we also said to ourselves no that the patients have been settled in the new areas were they have been settled are visited there for instance the Culinnana rehab the one even in Friday evening. Consistently the team has been visiting the facilities
Devi: I hear you but it boggles my mind that you have a completely different end of the stick that’s what Boggles my mind
MEC: but remember I’m not dismissing you what I’m saying to you, you have a different information please share it with me so that
Debbie: I will share it with you, that’s the point
MEC: deal with it
Debbie: but also you must remember we are dealing with mental health patients here who cannot necessarily speak for themselves
MEC: and I’m fully aware of that and I know my responsibility and that of the department

07:16 Devi: Mark Haywood the executive director at Section 27 has been working closely with the patients and families to slow down the process since 2015.
07:25 Mark: Yes the MEC knew she was told repeatedly about peoples fears, she was told repeatedly that this could cause a disaster. She went full steam ahead into the disaster with her eyes wide open knowing that that train was probably going to crash and thankfully not appearing to give a damn about it.

07:47 Devi: on the day the ombudsman release is report the MEC resigned but he is in support of a criminal investigation into the matter also recommended that key players like the HOD Dr. Sello and the Director DR. Manamela all faced disciplinary action and suspension and a full review of all 27 NGO’s resulting in closure of those found to be substandard.
08:10 Mar: 1300 people were moved out of Life Esidimeni, we know that 94 people died we know that 1300 minus 94 gives you 1200 people left who are somewhere and what if its another 100 or 200 or 300 people who are still in life threatening circumstances as we speak
08:32 Devi: And what is happening to some of the people who are still at these NGO's?
Minister: well for your information as I’m speaking, the DG the Director General of the department and the DG in the Premier office they are already visiting those NGO’s but remember there are 27 we must, their licenses were all invalid. The reason why they were invalid is because a director of mental health who doesn’t have the legal powers issued them. That’s were the word invalid comes from, if it was us we would have issued it. If no then it must be closed but if yes then you see where the other problems and fix them.

09:15 Rev: Heavenly Father we thank you for this day…
I’m very much angry, much angry with department of health, angry with the NGO’s and all the stakeholders under the umbrella of health.
089:37 Christine: They need to be charged, the MEC needs to be charged, this is for me this is Murder. This is just simple murder.
09:48 Mark: if I was the Minister of Police or Commissioner for Police in Gauteng I would be calling my people and say “ hey a massacre took place here we have to find out what was behind this massacre ” that’s what I would be doing they shouldn’t need to be asked, to do that they should be doing that.

Consistently the team has been visiting the facilities Devi: I hear you but it boggles my mind that you have a completely different end of the stick that’s what Boggles my mind MEC: but remember I’m not dismissing you what I’m saying to you, you have a different information please share it with me so that Debbie: I will share it with you, that’s the point MEC: deal with it Debbie: but also you must remember we are dealing with mental health patients here who cannot necessarily speak for themselves MEC: and I’m fully aware of that and I know my responsibility and that of the department 07:16 Devi: Mark Haywood the executive director at Section 27 has been working closely with the patients and families to slow down the process since 2015. 07:25 Mark: Yes the MEC knew she was told repeatedly about peoples fears, she was told repeatedly that this could cause a disaster. Manamela all faced disciplinary action and suspension and a full review of all 27 NGO’s resulting in closure of those found to be substandard. 08:10 Mar: 1300 people were moved out of Life Esidimeni, we know that 94 people died we know that 1300 minus 94 gives you 1200 people left who are somewhere and what if its another 100 or 200 or 300 people who are still in life threatening circumstances as we speak 08:32 Devi: And what is happening to some of the people who are still at these NGO's? Minister: well for your information as I’m speaking, the DG the Director General of the department and the DG in the Premier office they are already visiting those NGO’s but remember there are 27 we must, their licenses were all invalid. This is just simple murder. 09:48 Mark: if I was the Minister of Police or Commissioner for Police in Gauteng I would be calling my people and say “ hey a massacre took place here we have to find out what was behind this massacre ” that’s what I would be doing they shouldn’t need to be asked, to do that they should be doing that.

metadata.Further information: Link: As part of a program to deinstitutionalize mentally ill patients and cut costs between the 1st of April and the 30th of June 2016, the Gauteng MEC for Health Qedani Mahlangu moved an estimated 1371 mentally ill patients from Life Esidimeni to 27 NGO’s and various hospitals with catastrophic results. When we brought you the story last July we were shocked by what we had uncovered, but the findings released by the health Ombud on the 1st of February this year have left South Africa silenced. 94 mentally ill patients have died, due to a series of events that could have largely been avoided. And now we are asking who will be held accountable?
